messages.subject: Equality constraints on forced estimates
parts:
Dear group, 

I am currently having trouble specifying an alternative identification strategy for longitudinal measurement invariance testing (Widaman, 2010). The part that seems not work is forcing the first item at T1 loading to be estimated freely (I used NA for this) and at the same time constraining the first item loading at T2 to be equal to the first item at T1 (I used equal("") for this). 

Here is a minimal working example using the PoliticalDemocracy dataset. 

library(lavaan)
mod_wid<-'
  demo60 =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
  demo65 =~ equal("demo60=~y1")*y5 + y6 + y7 + y8
  y1 ~~ y5
  y2 ~~ y6
  y3 ~~ y7
  y4 ~~ y8
  demo60 ~ 0*1
  demo60 ~~ 1*demo60
  demo65 ~ NA*1
  demo65 ~~ NA*demo65
  y1 ~ NA*1
  y5 ~ equal("y1 ~ 1")*1
'

fit_wid<-cfa(mod_wid, PoliticalDemocracy, auto.fix.first=F)
summary(fit_wid)


When I run this code (lavaan version 0.5-23.1097) the model will be estimated, however, the estimated loadings for the items y1 and y5 seem to be fixed to 1. I also tried providing an explicit label but to no avail. 

Any help is much apprecciated

Gerrit

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Equality constraints on forced estimates
parts:
This syntax does not scale demo65. You cannot both free its variance and not fix a loading. Set the variance of demo65 to 1, just like demo60, and that may solve the problem.
     You know, you can refer to the same coefficient multiple times. So you could say
demo60 =~ NA*y1 + a*y1 + ...
and thus use simpler labels to impose equality constraints.

messages.author: 1d708274f571721f
messages.subject: Re: Equality constraints on forced estimates
parts:
Dear Ed,

thanks a lot for the swift response. Yes, the idea was to scale demo65 by fixing the loading via the equality constraint. 

Your tip that one can use address the same coefficient multiple times was spot on. 

So - for future reference - the code below implements this strategy and yields - as it should - identical fit indices. 

mod_wid<-'
  demo60 =~ NA*y1 + a*y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
  demo65 =~ NA*y5 + a*y5 + y6 + y7 + y8

y1 ~~ y5
  y2 ~~ y6
  y3 ~~ y7
  y4 ~~ y8
  demo60 ~ 0*1
  demo60 ~~ 1*demo60
  demo65 ~ NA*1
  demo65 ~~ NA*demo65
  y1 ~ NA*1
  y5 ~ equal("y1 ~ 1")*1
'

cfa(mod_wid, PoliticalDemocracy, auto.fix.first=F)

Best 
Gerrit
